answer: In an EigenTrust-style network, reputation decays exponentially with a defined half-life, so trust must be renewed through sustained honest service rather than accumulated once and retained indefinitely. A freshly spawned Sybil identity has near-zero eigenvector centrality and little reciprocal support; its influence cannot ripple through trusted peers enough to cross the consensus threshold. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity forms a reef against fabricated trust, while the terrace of established ratings remains costly to imitate.
